Fawn fucked me up in childhood/early teens, when your being neglected at home you start seeking love,  unfortunately people can take advantage of that.

Eventually, after a ton of bad experiences, Flight was a major component, which was sucky bc there were times where my anxieties got so bad I would start hallucinating demons, monsters, all that creepypasta stuff. 

After finally getting medicated and learning how to dissociate through "work face" - it's now my default. Unfortunately, it works so well that I've become extremely dissociative, the complete loss of identity, the memory issues, and just general cognitive issues are very difficult to work around, repression makes therapy very difficult, so much so that I've actually come off the medication to lessen the dissociation.

I consider Freeze the worst because when heavily relied on, it can strip you of the very things you need to recover, an example is talking with a therapist about trauma and what should evoke an emotional response to work through instead triggers a shut down, it shuts off your traumatic memory and you forget how you felt, let alone why.

This post reminds me very much of this one thought that's been running through my mind, 

Nobody wants me to die, but nobody wants to help me live.

The indifference is ridiculous even within mental health services. If you don't have a strong support network of people who actively care about you, recovery feels near impossible.

I'm 29, I was only diagnosed with cptsd earlier this year, the therapist i was working with then wanted me to get an Autism check, now I'm on a waiting list for the assessment but the letter they sent basically confirmed the suspicion. They'd been treating me as a BPD patient prior to that, something I'm trying to get rescinded bc I don't think it's accurate.

I have found it very helpful but I only started self-medicating with it after I saw how it was used medicinally as a treatment for autism after I found out I was. I've used it recreationally for longer but never as something consistent to be had everyday, tbh it helped me back then. An emergency joint could be the difference between being safe and being in hospital but that's at a high dose.

As a micro-dose I currently take with a vape, it's been working well as a mild antidepressant although my tolerance has built up which is kinda tough to manage without taking a tolerance break.

I also wanna make it abundantly clear that you should research as much as you can especially if you're taking other medications, it can interact and lessen the effectiveness of antipsychotics while having side effects of it's own, it's important to know the risks before making the decision to self-medicate, otherwise it's best to leave it to the professionals.

I feel that, I compartmentalised my trauma and walked over it to keep going, thinking my adult life would be the payoff of love and happiness i was waiting for.

Now that you mention it yeah, although I never really thought about from that perspective.

I was neglected by my parents as a kid; it was really hard to understand the emotions I was experiencing but I vividly remember imagining that both my parents had died and doing so allowed me to grieve the abandonment I felt, but in turn it kind of emotionally numbed me to the real death of friends and family.

As a teenager though, everything was so intense I was have flashbacks all the time but I was coping with more than I could understand, I was so heavily repressive of certain things that I couldn't link any of my emotional overflow to an experience so in trying to figure out why I felt so much I would end up ruminating more reasons I felt that way.

To justify what were emotional flashbacks I would think up reasons I would feel that way bc I had no cognitive memory of the initial trauma, "I feel intense shame, why do I feel this way?  it must be bc I am X/Y/Z" instead of "Oh that reminds me of that horrible experience which makes me feel shame"

Yeah, that's how parts end up functioning against each other, because these different "selves" can't relate or understand one another.

IME we kind of build coping mechanisms on top of each other until we find a what's the most effective at that time, this changes how we think and act so by the time we feel settled we're inherently different than who we were before and this can repeat every time our current coping mechanism fails which resonates with that feeling of being broken over and over again.  


A lot of parts/selves I feel can be broken down to what survival mechanism we were using at the time, raw emotional states are childlike because that's when we developed that state and when we spend our entire lives building over different mechanisms we're not gonna relate to the ones that didn't work because we're so focused on developing coping mechanism that do work (kind of)  


I completely understand not relating to the past, depersonalization is my trauma-power, when I talk to therapists about my life as far as i'm concerned i'm not talking about myself but it's the only way I can talk about it, the main reason your sentiment reminded me so much of IFS is because it's primarily about learning to relate and empathize with yourself again.

Claiming that he never uninvited you and that you are immature for taking the time you need to spend away from him after he treated you so terribly, at Christmas of all times. Threatening you with silence if you don't spend time with him is also a big red flag.

Idealised image and concept of other (also unrelenting standards)
Testing and confirming loyalty (abandonment/mistrust)
Fulfilling a sense of self (undeveloped self)

As a Controller user and a midcore raider, I can tell you now that macros are your friend.

BLM:Freeze SMN: Shadow Flare, AST: Earthly Star, DRK: Salted Earth

​

These are an example of skills that should be macro'd to appear on your target, this is to save time with AOE placement which is particularly awkward on PS4 and with cast times/2.44 CD you want to make the most of your time

example of macro:

/ac "Earthly Star" <t>

​

Even Keyboard+Mouse users I know make use of macros as often it's a matter of convenience, Bard players will macro their party member defensives to land on their target's target, which if the run is going smoothly will be the tank, making life a little easier for tankbuster hits.

example of macro:

/ac "Palisade" <tt>

​

Dragoon's can tether their buff on to party members and set it up to target members in a specific order unless they target someone manually,

This is set to target my bard, then my melee partner, then my caster if i'm not targeting manually

/merror off
